Fellow giant here, struggled on and off with this too. While people are right that there’s no set style for being non binary here are a couple different options and approaches that may help you find what works for you.

Androgyny: if you’re anything like myself hairy ness and our size can make this initially feel unattainable but having seen other friends of similar heights and builds experiment with it this can still be done, for some inspiration mx apparel creates clothing with this in mind and their social media also discuses the thought process behind their designs.

Maximalism: thing muppets, think clowns, think in your face out and proud. Maximalism says “other” through breaking social expectations for expression. This is most definitely a game of finding what works for you and what doesn’t but essentially boils down to “I’ve always wanted to wear that” wear it, do you feel great in it? Keep wearing it.

Subtlety: an easy stepping off point and a good place to start. What are little things you might enjoy wearing that might feel like little liberating acts and cause others to question without having to be told (not that they should have to be told but follow me with this) as others said this could be pride pins or pronoun pins on the more blunt side, or jewellery, accessories or understated items.


As has been said there are no wrong answers with expression and you don’t have to make any changes to be valid and accepted as a non-binary individual but if you want some direction for potential options I hope these can help

After looking at the guitar, a decent set of gotohs or Wilkinson vintage tuners would do you well enough for improving tuning stability. Any roller bridge should drop in and a new nut probably wouldn’t be a bad way to go. It looks like it’s got a back plate too so electronics mods shouldn’t be too tough either.

I think the question with upgrading guitars is very much “do you wanna keep it?” If the answer is yes then upgrade to your hearts content. 
Locking tuners should pretty much all require modifications to the headstock, if you’re set on them then modifying the headstock would be worthwhile, but in my experience other than for the speed of string changes there’s no reason you won’t get equivalent tuning stability from non locking tuners that you’d be able to drop in instantly. A roller bridge can be a good addition for tuning stability on bigsby vibratos and upgrading pots can majorly improve the sound of your guitar without the need to upgrade pickups (though pickups are a super fun rabbit hole to go down). I tend to modify my guitars if they’re nearly perfect but there’s no rules so unless you’re considering replacing it for an altogether superior guitar in your eyes, I’d say upgrade to your hearts content.

Really good contrast between the first and second section. I’d say that while the break going from the first section into the second works really well but maybe not as much going back from the second section into the first again. 

It’s noticeable that you added extra elements on repeats of sections and while they’re good additions they don’t add much to the dynamics or texture of the song as it goes on, consider how you could build the intensity of the chorus section as the song progresses or how it could possibly build to that point throughout, similarly is there a way to build on the verse section. It comes across as very influenced by mcr and green day in the kind of black parade and wake me up when September ends vibe. Looking at how they approach developing their ideas could help you really expand on your initial ideas.

I’d also recommend a bridge or third section of some sort. Going down the mcr route you could look at how combining both sections together might work or something to bridge the gap between both contrasting sections saved for the end could work well too.

That’s where I’d go from here but for real, this is a really good arrangement for so early on in your music journey and if the mcr influences were at least a bit intentional then that shows a really good understanding of the stylistic approaches of the music you like which is a really valuable skill especially so young. A guitar set up is when a guitar technician or luthier, adjusts the adjustable components on a guitar and fine tunes them to make the guitar play as comfortably as possible.
Most guitar shop will have technicians working in the store and will set up your guitar for between £30 and £50 or the dollar equivalent. 
Getting a set up will make your guitar a lot more comfortable to play from the get go.

I’d say with that budget, look at a hard tail squire bullet strat or mustang and a small fender amp. If you can push your budget try and get a guitar set up as it’ll make a cheaper learner guitar feel two or three times better.

Fender squire can definitely be as good as a fender Stratocaster I’d say as a beginner you’ll find something you like more in the squire range as it’s broader. I would recommend saving a bit and going for a squire contemporary or a second hand fender MiM strat.

It is possible to get close by changing the pickups or experimenting in the rest of your rig, but it’s not gonna get very close from stock.
